qa_pairs.question: What are the key registration, class, add/drop, census, withdrawal, and final examination dates for Fall 2026?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For Fall 2026, priority registration opens July 20, regular registration closes August 14, classes begin August 17, standard add/drop ends at 17:00 on August 28, census is September 4, the last day to withdraw with a W is October 30, and final examinations run December 7 through December 12.

contexts.text: For Fall 2026, priority registration opens on July 20, regular registration closes on August 14, classes begin on August 17, and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. qa_pairs.question: What are the undergraduate tuition rate and student-services fees for the 2026–2027 academic year?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition is USD 420 per registered credit. The student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall and Spring and USD 90 in Summer.

contexts.text: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit. The student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall and Spring and USD 90 in Summer. Tuition and mandatory fees are due by the regular registration deadline listed in `01_academic_calendar.md`. A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

qa_pairs.question: What is Northstar's attendance threshold, and what happens after three consecutive unexplained absences?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A syllabus may set a higher but not a lower threshold. Three consecutive unexplained absences trigger an academic-support alert, which is not itself a disciplinary finding.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold. Three consecutive unexplained absences trigger an academic-support alert; the alert itself is not a disciplinary finding.

qa_pairs.question: What academic requirements must an undergraduate meet to be eligible to graduate?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An undergraduate must complete at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00. Unless an approved exchange agreement says otherwise, at least 30 of the final 45 applicable credits must be completed at Northstar University.

contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00. At least 30 of the final 45 applicable credits must be completed at Northstar University unless an approved exchange agreement states otherwise.

qa_pairs.question: What should a student do if they suspect their Northstar account has been compromised?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk. If payment fraud is suspected, they should also report it to Student Accounts and their payment provider. They should never give staff a password or one-time authentication code.

contexts.text: Northstar uses the student portal and university email for official account communication. Multi-factor authentication is required for the portal. Staff will never request a password or one-time authentication code. A student who suspects account compromise should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk. Suspected payment fraud should also be reported to Student Accounts and the student's payment provider.

qa_pairs.question: After standard add/drop but before census, what must a student do to complete a late add, and when is the fee refundable?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student needs instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Late add is available only through census, and failure to pay on time cancels it. The fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

contexts.text: Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add. The fee and any additional tuition are described in `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.

The late-add fee is USD 40 per course and must be paid within two business days after the approvals described in `02_course_registration.md`. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: What academic and conduct conditions must a Northstar Merit Scholarship recipient meet for renewal, and what happens after a first academic failure?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction. A first failure of one academic renewal requirement normally results in one term of scholarship probation while the award stays active, but a serious-conduct sanction may end the award immediately.

contexts.text: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction. Pass/fail courses count toward the credit load only when the student earns a pass, but they do not contribute grade points to GPA.

A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term. A serious-conduct sanction may end the award immediately and is not protected by the academic probation rule.

qa_pairs.question: For Fall 2026, what are the academic and tuition consequences of withdrawing from one course on October 15?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: October 15 is after the September 4 census date but before the October 30 withdrawal deadline, so the course receives a W. For an ordinary course withdrawal after census, no tuition is reversed. The W may remain part of attempted-credit calculations.

contexts.text: The census date is September 4. The last day to withdraw from a course with a `W` grade is October 30, and final examinations run from December 7 through December 12.

Dropping one or more courses while remaining enrolled is a course withdrawal. Before or on census, the portal records a drop. After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`. After that deadline, withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition. Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.

For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal. Mandatory term fees are refundable only when the student withdraws from every course before classes begin.

qa_pairs.question: A student believes a final grade contains a calculation error. What steps and deadlines apply to the grade appeal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. They may then file a formal grade appeal within ten business days after publication and identify a permitted ground such as calculation error. The department chair reviews first; a further appeal to the Academic Review Panel is available within five business days only for new material evidence or a documented procedural error.

contexts.text: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor. Alleged calculation error, procedural unfairness, discrimination, or inconsistency with the published syllabus may proceed to the formal grade-appeal route in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

A grade appeal is different from a service complaint. The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

The department chair reviews a grade appeal first. A student may appeal the chair's outcome to the Academic Review Panel within five business days only when there is new material evidence or a documented procedural error in the first review. The Panel's decision is final within the university process.

qa_pairs.question: What must a student complete for a required internship, including approvals, hours, and post-placement submissions?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must complete at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, they need an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor; hours completed before approval normally do not count. The supervisor submits a completion evaluation, and the student submits the programme reflection within ten business days after the placement ends. Hours may be split across two approved placements, each with its own agreement.

contexts.text: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor. Hours completed before approval do not normally count. The supervisor submits a completion evaluation, and the student submits the programme reflection within ten business days after the placement ends. A student may split the hours across two approved placements, but each placement requires its own agreement.

qa_pairs.question: How do approved medical leave and voluntary leave for employment or travel affect a Northstar Merit Scholarship?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not use the one-term probation opportunity. Voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the scholarship; the student must request a deferral before census. A standard leave request must be submitted before census with a reason, required documentation, and programme approval.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. Scholarship decisions may be appealed within ten business days using the process in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

A leave of absence pauses active enrolment while preserving the student's programme place. A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval. Employment, travel, family responsibilities, and health circumstances may support a request, but approval is not automatic.

qa_pairs.question: A student has completed all academic graduation requirements but still has an unpaid balance. Can the degree and final transcript be released?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. An unpaid balance after the grace period creates a financial hold. Although the hold does not erase completed academic requirements, it blocks graduation clearance, official degree conferral, and release of the final transcript until resolved.

contexts.text: An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed. A payment plan is available for balances of at least USD 1,000; it requires 40% by the original due date and two equal monthly instalments. Missing an instalment creates a financial hold.

Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.

qa_pairs.question: A student discussed a late add in July 2026 but submits the request on August 3, 2026. Which policy applies, what is the fee, and how long is the window?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Registration Policy version 2.0 applies because the registration action occurs on or after August 1, 2026; discussing it in July does not invoke version 1.0. The request is allowed only from the end of standard add/drop through census, and the fee is USD 40 per course, payable within two business days after instructor and programme-director approvals.

contexts.text: Policy documents display a version and effective date. The policy in force on the triggering event date controls unless a newer policy explicitly states that it applies retroactively. A newer publication does not silently rewrite an earlier transaction. When the event spans multiple dates, use the date identified by the policy: for registration it is the registration action date, for tuition refunds it is the recorded drop or withdrawal date, and for scholarship review it is the end of the reviewed term.

Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.

Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add. The fee and any additional tuition are described in `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.

qa_pairs.question: A documented medical condition prevented a student from filing on time, and the student seeks retroactive withdrawal and money back. What deadlines and financial outcomes can apply?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A retroactive medical-leave request normally must be filed within 30 calendar days after the last documented participation. A later filing needs evidence that the condition also prevented filing during those 30 days. If medical withdrawal is approved, the student may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study based on the last documented participation date, not a cash refund. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

contexts.text: Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation. Later requests require evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period. Medical documentation should describe functional impact and relevant dates; it should not be emailed to individual instructors.

An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated. Students with scholarships must therefore review `04_scholarships.md`; a refund estimate shown before scholarship adjustment is not final.

qa_pairs.question: A student completed 75% of assessed work, was passing before a documented emergency, and can finish independently. What is required for an incomplete, what happens at the deadline, and can academic judgement alone be appealed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student may qualify for an I if the remaining conditions are met and the student and instructor sign an incomplete plan. The default completion deadline is the end of the next regular term; without a submitted grade or approved extension, the I becomes F. Academic judgement alone is not a permitted appeal ground, although calculation error, material departure from the syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination may support an appeal.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

A grade appeal is different from a service complaint. The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

qa_pairs.question: A student plans to return from approved leave for Spring 2027. By what date should the return notice be submitted, and what happens if the student misses the approved return term?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Spring 2027 regular registration closes January 8, 2027, so a return notice required at least 20 calendar days earlier should be submitted by December 19, 2026. contexts.text: For Spring 2027, priority registration opens on November 23, regular registration closes on January 8, classes begin on January 11, the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on January 22, and the census date is January 29. The last day to withdraw with a `W` is March 26. Final examinations run from May 3 through May 8.

To return from approved leave, a student submits a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes. A medical leave may include fitness-to-return conditions that were stated in the original approval. Failure to return by the approved term changes the status to inactive; readmission is then required.

qa_pairs.question: A parent who pays a student's tuition asks for the student's grades and wants to challenge one grade. What may Northstar disclose, and what process must be used?

Northstar may discuss the record only with the student or a person who has valid recorded authorization. contexts.text: The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization. A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information. Students may download their own enrolment and billing records from the portal. Requests to correct inaccurate personal data go to the Records Office; requests to change an academic decision must use the relevant appeal process.

A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. It may explain a rule, but it cannot approve an exception, change a grade, waive a fee, guarantee scholarship renewal, or access an individual student record.

After the census date, a course may be added only to correct a documented university administrative error. A student who stops attending without dropping or withdrawing remains enrolled and may receive a failing grade. Withdrawal rules are described in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`.
